plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn lavender-blue when this tree flowers. Clusters of trumpet-shaped blooms open on feathery, fern-like foliage. The petals then drop and carpet pavements and lawns in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking from October to November
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and Sydney and Brisbane, Australia
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America. Its blossom time is so famous in Pretoria that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub flowers when most gardens are fading. Its delicate, often lightly fragrant blooms open from late autumn and draw in the last foraging bees of the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter, roughly October to December
plants.location: Japan, where it is native, and mild temperate gardens in the southeastern United States and Europe
plants.funFact: The leaves of related camellias give us tea, and sasanqua seeds are pressed for camellia oil. The oil has long been used in cooking and hair care in Japan.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: This garden favorite flowers as the days shorten. It produces dense, layered pom-pom, spider and daisy-like heads that glow in cool autumn light, often lasting through the first light frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, peaking from October to November in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across Japan, China, Europe and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants, so they set buds only when nights grow long. Growers can control the bloom date with blackout cloth. Japan's imperial family uses the flower as its crest.
